extracted.intended_audience: Interested members of the public, potential litigants or their counsel, stakeholders in the U.S. 219 Meyersdale–Old Salisbury Road project, and other federal/state agencies
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Highway Administration notice announcing final agency actions for the U.S. 219 (Section 050) Transportation Improvement Project, including the judicial-review deadline, applicable authorities, where the FEIS/ROD and administrative record can be obtained, and the project's stated purpose and needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim seeking judicial review of the Federal agency actions on the highway project will be barred unless the claim is filed on or before November 3, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per 23 U.S.C. 139(l)(1). If the Federal law that authorizes judicial review provides a time period of less than 150 days for filing such claim, then that shorter time period still applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments acceptance status
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are no longer being accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the DATES section of the notice for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: FHWA final agency action and administrative record
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA has taken final agency action by issuing approval for the U.S. 6219, Section 050 Transportation Improvement Project; actions are described in the FHWA Final Environmental Impact Statement (FEIS), Record of Decision (ROD), and other documents in the FHWA administrative record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FEIS, ROD, and other administrative record files are available by contacting FHWA at the address provided (David Snyder, Interim Division Administrator) and can be viewed/downloaded from the project website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project purpose and needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: to complete Corridor N of the Appalachian Development Highway System, improve system linkage in the region, provide safe and efficient access for motorists traveling on U.S. 219, and provide transportation infrastructure to support economic opportunities in existing and planned communities and employment/business centers and natural resource-based industries within the Appalachian Region. The needs: existing U.S. 219 does not provide efficient mobility for trucks and freight; numerous roadway and geometric deficiencies present along existing alignment; existing roadway infrastructure limits economic development opportunities in the Appalachian Region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These purpose-and-need statements frame why the project was proposed and are reflected in the FEIS and ROD.
